notes.title: Dev report #5 ~ March update
notes.notes:
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44967334/651105de3d95ab6f83b2ce872928677b691bea30.png

Hello Explorers!

March has been packed with new content and some major improvements across the board.  
From visual upgrades to brand new gameplay systems, we’ve been focused on deepening the player experience and making each run through Chaos Islands feel more exciting.

Let’s take a look at everything that was added last month!

Boss Buffs

To make boss fights more dynamic and challenging, we added a set of  
new randomized buffs that can appear on bosses during encounters:


Berserker – Deals more damage when low on health.
Regenerator – Restores health points at the start of each turn.
Aggressor – Attacks deal 1.5× damage.
Beefy – Takes 25% reduced damage.
Hellborn – Resistant to fire damage.
Thick Skin – Max HP increased by 50%.  


New Enemies

We introduced several new enemy types last month, expanding the range of challenges players will face:

Infested + zulk  
Infested demon carries a parasite, zulk, that will be spawned after the host's death unless the player uses special cards or defensive constructions to prevent that.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44967334/1d682264633eedaaa07615dd5ae4a566c87c2d19.png

We also had a funny bug during the development of that enemy – accidentally we created a very powerful boss.

[previewyoutube=MarWOjiW5iM;full][/previewyoutube]

Summoner  
A dangerous and beefy enemy that can summon reinforcements if the player does not deal with him quickly.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44967334/c259eef002cf16dd6ebda20c7993c4cdf3b5e477.png

Necromancer  
Their job is to bring the dead back to life using pile of bones – and create chaos on the battlefield.

When enemies die, they now leave behind a Pile of Bones.  
If necromancer units are present (or arrive later), they can use these piles to  
resurrect fallen enemies.

In some battles, bone piles may even be placed on the field before combat starts.  
So players will have to take care of them before the battle to avoid a bigger threat.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44967334/baf3d5a77540569edafd1448956be281b1cd5617.png

Node Map Updates

We continued developing the node map by adding new mechanics as well as slowly improving visual style.

What's New:
  
Playable Nodes - These are nodes that launch an actual game session, requiring players to complete an in-game challenge to proceed.
Event Nodes were implemented. These offer narrative-style choices - some helpful, some... not so much.
Locks & Keys Some paths will be locked and require keys to unlock - so players will have to do some exploration in order to find a key or another path.  


{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44967334/4c7492ac7eff496280b7984208530ed4797f4226.png

New Environment: Lake Tile

To break up the chaos with some serenity, we added a Lake tile type.  
Expect to find this peaceful feature on some islands during your journey.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44967334/9499369d3515c8d111a6c35d583e0efa48e4f996.png

And that’s all for this month! We’ll continue expanding enemy types, balancing the new gameplay systems, and preparing more progression surprises in the coming month!

➡️ We encourage you to join our Discord.  
We are posting updates each week and we would like to chat with you :)

Until next time!

notes.title: Dev report #4 ~ February update
notes.notes:
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44967334/651105de3d95ab6f83b2ce872928677b691bea30.png


Hello everyone!

Welcome to this month’s Chaos Islands Dev Report! Over the past few weeks, we’ve been hard at work improving the game, refining its systems, and introducing new content. Here’s what we’ve been up to!

Progression System Updates

Progression is a core aspect of Chaos Islands, and we’ve made significant strides in developing its mechanics.


 The node generation algorithm is now complete! This was a crucial step in designing the game’s progression system, allowing us to create a dynamic and engaging experience for players.
 With the algorithm in place, we’ve started working on player movement mechanics, different node types, and interaction mechanics to bring the system to life and showcase them on incoming playtests.
 Additionally, we are constantly working on improving the visuals, ensuring they fit seamlessly into the evolving gameplay experience.


{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44967334/b3289ea8c06e945e8fb3d5f72f567761bff7eac8.png

Enhancing UX and UI

Improving player experience is always a priority, and we’ve made a few key adjustments:


 Card Descriptions - We’ve enhanced card descriptions by adding icons and refining the design to make their effects clearer.
 Season UI - While season effects were already present in the buffs section, playtesters often overlooked them. To address this, we’ve introduced a new UI element near the season clock, ensuring players can easily see the current season’s impact.
 We’ve also fixed several bugs discovered during recent playtests, leading to a smoother gameplay experience.


{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44967334/2683ac12efa3599f4a7e160304e2d98e0d410305.png

New Enemies Enter the Fray!

Combat is getting more intense with the addition of several new enemy types, each bringing unique mechanics to challenge players:


 Shaman – Places demonic wards around the map to boost other demons.
 Infested – Spawns an Imp upon death.
 Imp – A smaller, more agile version of the Minion demon.
 Summoner – Continuously spawns Imps around itself.
 Lich – Has the ability to revive fallen demons, making battles even more unpredictable.
 Bomber – Explodes upon death, dealing damage to surrounding tiles.


We are also working on additional demon types, which we hope to reveal in the near future!

New Defense Constructions

To counter these new threats, we’ve introduced powerful defensive structures to aid players in battle:


 Ice Tower – Freezes enemies for a few turns.
 Fire Tower – Sets enemies and surrounding tiles on fire.


These defenses come with a fun interaction mechanic: fire cancels ice and vice versa. Additionally, the Fire Tower won’t be as effective during rain or snowstorms, adding another layer of strategy to the game!

What’s Next?

As development continues, we’re focused on refining progression, introducing more engaging enemies, and improving gameplay balance. We can’t wait to share more with you in our next updates!

Thank you for your continued support and feedback—it truly helps us shape Chaos Islands into the best game it can be.
